E.label: row2/28: top vs side planes
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.rect(40, 40); const b = sketch('side'); b.rect(10, 10); loft(a, b, 30);
E.sentence: The two sketches are on different planes ('top' and 'side'), so there is no single direction to loft along; draw both on the same plane.

E.label: row28: top vs front planes
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.rect(40, 40); const b = sketch('front'); b.rect(10, 10); loft(a, b, 30);
E.sentence: The two sketches are on different planes ('top' and 'front'), so there is no single direction to loft along; draw both on the same plane.

E.label: row22/23: 5-corner square -> 4-corner rect
E.sentence: The first sketch has 5 corners and the second has 4, but a loft needs the same number on both, so delete any point that sits in the middle of a straight side.

E.label: row22: triangle -> square
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.polygon([[0,0],[40,0],[20,30]]); const b = sketch('top'); b.rect(10, 10); loft(a, b, 20);
E.sentence: The first sketch has 3 corners and the second has 4, but a loft needs the same number on both, so delete any point that sits in the middle of a straight side.

E.label: row20: square 40 -> square 20 twisted 20 deg
E.sentence: Matching sides of these two sketches are up to 20 degrees from parallel, which would twist the loft, so make each side of the first parallel to its partner in the second.

E.label: row20: square 40 -> square 40 twisted 2 deg
E.sentence: Matching sides of these two sketches are up to 2 degrees from parallel, which would twist the loft, so make each side of the first parallel to its partner in the second.

E.label: row11: regular triangle r20 -> circle(40)
E.sentence: A circle can only be lofted to another circle, an axis-aligned rectangle (long side at most twice the short side), or a regular 4, 5, 6 or 8 sided shape with a corner pointing right, and the other outline is none of those.

E.label: row24: hexagon turned 0.3 rad -> circle(40)
E.sentence: A circle can only be lofted to another circle, an axis-aligned rectangle (long side at most twice the short side), or a regular 4, 5, 6 or 8 sided shape with a corner pointing right, and the other outline is none of those.

E.label: row8: tiny circles r0.05 gap 300
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.circle(0.1); const b = sketch('top'); b.circle(0.1); loft(a, b, 300);
E.sentence: The larger circle has a radius of 0.05 mm, and a loft needs at least 0.5 mm to be built exactly, so make it bigger.

E.label: row8: circles r0.5 gap 100
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.circle(1); const b = sketch('top'); b.circle(1); loft(a, b, 100);
E.sentence: The larger circle (radius 0.5 mm) is under 1/40 of the loft's overall size (100 mm), which cannot be built exactly; make the circle bigger or the gap smaller.

E.label: row26: gap 0
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.rect(40, 40); const b = sketch('top'); b.rect(10, 10); loft(a, b, 0);
E.sentence: The two sketches are in the same place (the gap is zero), so there is nothing between them to fill; give the loft a gap above zero.

E.label: row27: loft(a, a, 30)
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.rect(40, 40); const b = sketch('top'); b.rect(10, 10); loft(a, a, 30);
E.sentence: The loft was given the same sketch twice, so both of its ends would be in the same place whatever gap you type; draw a second sketch for the other end.

E.label: row29: frame-placed sketches, gap ignored
E.sentence: The first sketch is placed with its own origin and direction, which a loft cannot combine with its gap, so draw both sketches on 'top', 'front' or 'side' and give the distance as the gap.

E.label: row30: datum height contradicts the gap
E.src: const a = sketch(plane('top', 0)); a.rect(40, 40); const b = sketch(plane('top', 30)); b.rect(20, 20); loft(a, b, 10);
E.sentence: The second sketch was placed at height 30, but the loft's gap puts it at 10, so make the two agree by changing the gap or the height the sketch was drawn at.

E.label: row35: undrawn second sketch
E.src: const a = sketch('top'); a.rect(40, 40); const b = sketch('top'); loft(a, b, 30);
E.sentence: The second sketch has not been drawn yet, so the loft would use the default 40 by 25 rectangle; draw its outline first, for example with rect(20, 20).
